back: Every measure has one, set by Tableau when you connect to a data source. For numeric measures it is usually a sum, so dropping the field gives `SUM(Field)`.

front: How do you change a measure's aggregation for one view?
back: Open the pill's menu and choose another aggregation under Measure. It affects that pill only.

front: How do you change a measure's default aggregation for the whole workbook?
back: In the Data pane, right-click the measure and choose Default Properties > Aggregation.
Returns the value if it has a single value for all rows in the group, otherwise it shows an asterisk (*). The asterisk is not an error in the data.

front: What does Analysis > Aggregate Measures do when cleared?
back: The view is disaggregated: Tableau shows a separate mark for every data value in every row. It is not the same as adding a dimension or a filter.
The combinations of dimension members in the view. They decide how the rows are grouped, and each group becomes one mark.

front: What happens to a total when you add a dimension to the view?
back: Tableau computes the measure again once per member. You get more marks, each with a smaller value.

front: Does a dimension on Color change the numbers?
back: Yes. A dimension on Color, Size, Label or Detail increases the number of marks without adding headers, just like one on Rows or Columns.
Adds a dimension to the level of detail without colour, size or headers. For example, one circle per member in a scatterplot.
